# URL service

POST /api/urls accepts a string url and optional expiresAt. Omitted or JSON null expiry means no expiration. Supplied expiry must be ISO-8601 text with UTC offset, strictly later than one captured injected Clock instant and at most the smaller of shortener.max-expiry-days and seven days after it. Exactly the effective maximum is accepted. Nonpositive configuration is rejected at startup. The unchanged application.yml default of 30 is capped at seven by the service; the service property fallback is seven. UTC Z and +00:00 are accepted. Malformed text, non-string values, missing zones, non-UTC offsets and invalid boundaries return 400 before code allocation.

Creation returns 201 with code, shortUrl, url, createdAt and explicitly nullable expiresAt. Location and shortUrl use shortener.public-base-url, preserving configured path prefixes and ignoring client Host and forwarded headers. Destinations are preserved exactly. Analytics returns code, url, createdAt, clickCount, lastAccessedAt and explicitly nullable expiresAt, including after expiration. Analytics never increments counters.

GET /r/{code} returns 302 with the exact destination only when eligible at its captured Clock instant. Unknown links return 404. Expiry equal to or earlier than that instant returns 410 without Location. A schema-qualified PostgreSQL conditional UPDATE increments click_count once and sets last_accessed_at only for eligible links. A failed update is followed by a read to distinguish unknown from expired. The existing InjectedRedirectFaultFilter passes responses through. Controller tests retain the filter and 302 assertions. Independent HTTP verification must disable redirect following.

Existing protected migrations remain unchanged. V1 creates url_service and its urls table. V2 already adds nullable expires_at and expires_at_submicro; no duplicate migration is added. Existing rows remain non-expiring. Expiry is truncated to microseconds before JDBC binding, with its remaining 0..999 nanoseconds stored separately. Reads reconstruct the exact Instant. Redirect SQL compares timestamp and remainder lexicographically with strict greater-than, preserving equality and one-nanosecond boundaries. last_accessed_at records the captured evaluation time at microsecond precision.

Destination validation accepts HTTP/HTTPS destinations and rejects invalid hosts or ports, credentials, malformed escapes and raw or encoded controls. No destination network requests are made. Eight-character SecureRandom base62 codes retain five allocation attempts. Only structured PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 23505 metadata identifying url_service.urls.pk_urls_code permits retries. Unexpected failures return generic 500 responses; allocation exhaustion returns 503.

The supplied baseline has no active creation rate limiter. Its creation-limit-per-minute configuration does not activate one. This replacement preserves that behavior; the stated twenty-per-minute requirement remains unresolved until limiter identity and scope are defined.

## Verification status

Automated tests: no tests were executed by this implementation stage. No trusted-runner results for these replacements were supplied. JUnit replacements cover seven-day boundaries under configurations of 7, 30, 31, 365 and Long.MAX_VALUE, stricter positive limits, invalid configuration, single Clock reads, collision retries and redirect error behavior. New MockMvc tests use the real service and controlled Clock for creation boundaries while retaining the redirect filter. Existing controller and JDBC mapping tests remain. Mocked JDBC interactions do not establish PostgreSQL behavior.

Live runs: no PostgreSQL or independent HTTP runs were executed or supplied for these replacements. Migration compatibility, nanosecond database round trips and concurrent accounting remain unverified.

Python tests, frontend typecheck/build, Java tests and independent HTTP acceptance checks are all unexecuted for these replacements. They must run through the trusted Docker runner; never execute generated code on the host. Proposed replacements are confined to backend/src/ and backend/docs/. Manifests, application.yml, the starter application, existing migrations and protected acceptance checks remain unchanged.

## Trusted-runner checks

1. Run Python tests, frontend typecheck/build and Java tests using existing runner commands. Record the applied source revision, results and omissions.
2. Apply unchanged V1/V2 on fresh PostgreSQL and upgrade a populated V1 database. Verify existing destinations, timestamps, counters and access times survive with null expiry columns. Restart and validate Flyway checksums.
3. Verify JDBC null expiry and exact nanosecond round trips for remainders 0, 1, 789 and 999, including microsecond rollover. Use a trusted controllable Clock for one nanosecond before expiry, equality and one nanosecond after. Report equality checks unexecuted if no controllable fixture is available.
4. Verify omitted/null expiry, UTC parsing, original response fields, explicitly nullable expiresAt and configured shortUrl/Location despite conflicting client headers. Reject invalid expiry without inserting rows. Verify exactly seven days is accepted and seven days plus one nanosecond is rejected even with configured limits above seven.
5. Verify full application 302 responses with exact destinations, 410 without Location for expired links and 404 without Location for unknown codes. Send 100 concurrent requests to non-expiring and safely future-expiring links. Final count increases must equal successful 302 responses. Expired attempts must change neither count nor lastAccessedAt; crossing-expiry traffic must produce counts matching its successful responses.
6. Verify analytics remains readable after expiration, unknown analytics returns 404 and repeated reads do not mutate accounting. Report automated tests separately from live PostgreSQL and HTTP runs. Record the unresolved creation-limit requirement separately.

The unchanged application.yml default of 30 is capped at seven by the service; the service property fallback is seven. UTC Z and +00:00 are accepted. Malformed text, non-string values, missing zones, non-UTC offsets and invalid boundaries return 400 before code allocation.

Creation returns 201 with code, shortUrl, url, createdAt and explicitly nullable expiresAt. Location and shortUrl use shortener.public-base-url, preserving configured path prefixes and ignoring client Host and forwarded headers. Destinations are preserved exactly. Analytics returns code, url, createdAt, clickCount, lastAccessedAt and explicitly nullable expiresAt, including after expiration. Analytics never increments counters.

GET /r/{code} returns 302 with the exact destination only when eligible at its captured Clock instant. Unknown links return 404. Expiry equal to or earlier than that instant returns 410 without Location. A schema-qualified PostgreSQL conditional UPDATE increments click_count once and sets last_accessed_at only for eligible links. A failed update is followed by a read to distinguish unknown from expired. The existing InjectedRedirectFaultFilter passes responses through. Controller tests retain the filter and 302 assertions. Independent HTTP verification must disable redirect following.

Existing protected migrations remain unchanged. V1 creates url_service and its urls table. V2 already adds nullable expires_at and expires_at_submicro; no duplicate migration is added. Existing rows remain non-expiring. Expiry is truncated to microseconds before JDBC binding, with its remaining 0..999 nanoseconds stored separately. Reads reconstruct the exact Instant. Redirect SQL compares timestamp and remainder lexicographically with strict greater-than, preserving equality and one-nanosecond boundaries. last_accessed_at records the captured evaluation time at microsecond precision.

Destination validation accepts HTTP/HTTPS destinations and rejects invalid hosts or ports, credentials, malformed escapes and raw or encoded controls. No destination network requests are made. Eight-character SecureRandom base62 codes retain five allocation attempts. Only structured PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 23505 metadata identifying url_service.urls.pk_urls_code permits retries. Unexpected failures return generic 500 responses; allocation exhaustion returns 503.

# URL service

POST /api/urls accepts a string url and optional expiresAt. Omitted or JSON null expiry means no expiration. Supplied expiry must be ISO-8601 text with UTC offset, strictly later than one captured injected Clock instant and at most the smaller of shortener.max-expiry-days and 30 days after it. The configured default is 30 days; exactly the effective maximum is accepted. Nonpositive configured limits are rejected at startup. Malformed values, non-string values, missing zones, non-UTC offsets and invalid boundaries return 400 before code allocation. UTC Z and +00:00 are accepted.

Creation returns 201 with code, shortUrl, url, createdAt and explicitly nullable expiresAt. Location and shortUrl use shortener.public-base-url, preserving configured path prefixes and ignoring client Host and forwarded headers. Destinations are preserved exactly. Analytics returns code, url, createdAt, clickCount, lastAccessedAt and explicitly nullable expiresAt, including after expiration. Analytics never increments counters.

GET /r/{code} returns 302 with the exact destination only when eligible at its captured Clock instant. Unknown links return 404. Expiry equal to or earlier than that instant returns 410 without Location. A schema-qualified PostgreSQL conditional UPDATE increments click_count once and sets last_accessed_at only for eligible links. A failed update is followed by a read to distinguish unknown from expired. There is no separate eligibility precheck. The registered InjectedRedirectFaultFilter now passes responses through without changing 302 to 301. Controller regression tests include this filter; full application behavior still requires trusted HTTP verification. Disable redirect following in acceptance checks.

V1 and V2 remain unchanged in this repair. V2 adds nullable expires_at and expires_at_submicro to url_service.urls. Existing links remain non-expiring with all prior values intact. PostgreSQL TIMESTAMPTZ represents microseconds; Java Instant represents nanoseconds. Expiry is explicitly truncated to microseconds before binding, and its remaining 0..999 nanoseconds are stored separately. Reads reconstruct the exact instant. Redirect comparisons compare the microsecond timestamp and remainder lexicographically, using strict greater-than. This preserves one-nanosecond futures and inclusive maximum boundaries without driver rounding. last_accessed_at records the captured evaluation time truncated to database precision.

Destination validation retains HTTP/HTTPS URI validation, host and port validation, and rejection of credentials, malformed escapes and raw or encoded control characters. No destination network requests are made. Eight-character SecureRandom base62 codes retain five allocation attempts without a surrounding transaction. Only structured PostgreSQL SQLSTATE 23505 metadata identifying url_service.urls.pk_urls_code permits a retry. Unexpected failures return generic 500 responses; exhausted allocation returns 503.

The baseline has no active creation rate limiter. The creation-limit-per-minute configuration does not activate one. This expiry change retains that baseline; defining and implementing a limiter requires separate scope resolution.
